subject: Communication
title: Emotional Empathy: Feeling What They Feel
description: A 60-second lesson on Emotional Empathy: Feeling What They Feel.

hook.text: A baby cries in a room and every other baby starts crying. No one taught them.

buildup.text: Emotional empathy — also called affective empathy — is the automatic sharing of another person's emotional state.

discovery.text: Mirror neurons fire both when you perform an action and when you watch someone else perform it — creating a neural mirror.

twist.text: Too much emotional empathy causes empathic distress — you absorb others' pain until you burn out.

climax.text: Emotional empathy needs regulation. Feeling others' pain is a gift — but only if you can feel it without drowning in it.

punchline.text: We're born feeling each other's pain. The skill is surviving it.

quiz.question: What neural mechanism supports emotional empathy?
